title: Cross-SDK: connection keep-alive, pooling defaults and streaming backpressure ergonomics
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Define and implement consistent transport defaults and ergonomics across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs focused on: sensible request timeouts, connection pooling / keep-alive defaults, idle connection eviction, and streaming backpressure settings. Provide clear upgrade path, examples, and stability tests so client teams can rely on consistent behavior for long-lived streaming workloads and high-throughput request patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Default timeout settings are documented and applied consistently across SDKs (Python, TS, Go)
Connection pool and keep-alive defaults reduce tail latency regressions in microbenchmark by >=15% for typical RLHF workloads
Streaming API surfaces ergonomic backpressure primitives for JavaScript/TypeScript and Go; Python streaming example remains ergonomic for asyncio users
Migration guide and examples published in docs with sample env variables and config snippets
Regression tests added to SDK CI that simulate 1k concurrent short requests and 50 concurrent long-lived streams
tasks: Audit existing transport implementations in all SDKs and list differences (timeouts, keep-alive, max connections, idle eviction)
Propose consistent canonical defaults and environment variable overrides for each SDK
Implement changes in Python SDK: HTTPX/requests transport wrapper + async streaming tweaks
Implement changes in TypeScript SDK: fetch/undici/http2 transport + streaming backpressure API
Implement changes in Go SDK: net/http transport tuning + http2/gRPC keep-alive settings
Add unit and load tests to catch regressions and expose flaky behavior
Publish docs, migration notes, and example snippets for customers
Coordinate rollout: feature-flagged release, monitor metrics, and do gradual enablement per SDK
comments: 2026-02-15 Aisha Banerjee: Created ticket after triage meeting — customers have reported intermittent slow tail latency and socket exhaustion in high-throughput environments. Goal: make SDKs resilient by default.

2026-02-18 Luca Moretti: Preliminary audit complete — TS SDK uses Undici with a default maxSockets=Infinity pattern, Python uses HTTPX with a small pool unless explicitly configured, Go uses net/http default (100 idle) which behaves differently. Need unified guidance.
2026-02-22 Sofia Patel (PM): Please include migration notes for hosted customers who set custom env vars; ensure console docs show cost/latency tradeoffs.
2026-02-28 Design review: Added streaming ergonomics wireframes for JS consumer APIs — prefer readable stream + backpressure helper rather than exposing raw socket.

2026-03-04 Engineering update (Luca): Implemented Python change to default to a persistent HTTPX AsyncClient with keepalive=60s and pool_limits tuned; added config key 'REDWOOD_SDK_KEEPALIVE' for override. Running local perf harness.
2026-03-06 Perf results (internal): With new defaults, P95 token generation latency improved ~18% under 800 concurrent short requests. Need to run Go and TS equivalents.
2026-03-09 QA: Added integration test that opens 40 concurrent streaming chat sessions for 10 minutes; observed no socket leaks in instrumented run.
2026-03-10 Luca Moretti: Opening PRs for TS and Go; planning canary release for TS in SDK beta channel next week. Will publish examples after PR merge.
example_snippets:
Python (async) example:
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(keepalive_seconds=60, max_connections=100, request_timeout=30)
async with client.stream_chat(conversation_id) as stream:
    async for chunk in stream: print(chunk)
